summary: Backend + frontend testing for iteration 2 (Welcome page + file upload). All 26 pytest backend tests pass (18 regression + 8 new upload tests). All frontend critical flows verified including Welcome page, admin image upload via Emergent object storage, /api/files/<id> serving, protected routing, register/login redirect to /home, and 9-card grid menu on dashboard. One minor UX deviation: logout redirects to /login instead of /.

issues: After clicking sb-logout-btn the app redirects to /login, while the PR spec stated it should land on '/' (Welcome). Both are valid UX patterns but should align with the spec — likely a one-line change in AuthContext/Sidebar logout handler (navigate('/') instead of navigate('/login')).

action_items: OPTIONAL/Minor: Align logout redirect with PR spec — currently goes to /login, PR expected '/' (Welcome). Update sb-logout-btn handler to navigate to '/'.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py now ~905 lines, growing further. Recommend splitting into modules: routers/(auth, courses, posts, videos, live, quizzes, notifications, files, contact, settings), models.py, storage.py, seed.py.

Storage key caching uses a module-level global and refreshes on 403 only — fine, but if the storage service returns 5xx, the key is not refreshed and the upload will fail without retry. Consider refreshing on any auth-related error.
/api/upload reads entire file into memory before size check. For large rejected files this still allocates RAM. Consider streaming + early abort on Content-Length, or using file.size when available.

/api/files/{file_id} streams the full object body through the FastAPI process (proxy pattern). For larger files (PDFs, videos) consider redirecting to a signed object-storage URL or using StreamingResponse with chunked iteration to avoid memory pressure.
No rate limiting on /api/upload — an authenticated user could upload many 5MB files. Consider per-user daily quota or rate limiter.
MIME validation is extension-based only — does not sniff actual content. A user could rename a .exe to .png and it would pass. For an Islamic education platform this is low risk but worth noting.
Logout endpoint deletes cookie but does not invalidate the JWT (JWT remains valid until exp). For sensitive sessions, maintain a server-side denylist.
Still no brute-force lockout on /api/auth/login (carry-over from iteration 1).

rca of the issue: Logout redirect mismatch RCA: PR spec states logout → '/'. Observation: after sb-logout-btn click, URL becomes /login. Reproduction: login as admin → open-sidebar-btn → sb-logout-btn → URL ends up at /login. Mitigation: in the logout handler (likely in AuthContext logout() or Sidebar's onClick), change navigate('/login') to navigate('/'). Since Welcome.jsx renders the landing page at '/' and itself redirects authenticated users to /home, '/' is the correct destination for guests.
